module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end

# packs-rails

`packs-rails` establishes and implements a set of conventions for splitting up large monoliths built on top of the [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) standard. `packs-rails` makes it easy to use [`packwerk`](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk) to modularize your rails app. With `packs-rails`, new packages' autoload paths are automatically added to Rails, so your code will immediately become usable and loadable without additional configuration.

Here is an example application that uses `packs-rails`:
```
package.yml # root level pack
app/ # Unpackaged code
  models/
  ...
packs/
  my_domain/
    package.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    package_todo.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    app/
      public/ # Recommended location for public API
        my_domain.rb # creates the primary namespaces
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain.rb
      services/ # Private services
        my_domain/
          some_private_class.rb
      models/ # Private models
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model.rb # this works too
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model.rb
      controllers/
      views/
    config/
      initializers/ # Initializers can live in packs and load as expected
    lib/
      tasks/
    spec/ # With packs-rails, specs for a pack live next to the pack
      public/
        my_domain_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain_spec.rb
      services/
        my_domain/
          some_private_class_spec.rb
      models/
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_spec.rb
      factories/ # packs-rails will automatically load pack factories into FactoryBot, see Ecosystem and Integrations#factory_bot below
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
  my_other_domain/
    ... # other packs have a similar structure
  my_other_other_domain/
    ...
```

## Usage

Setting up `packs-rails` is straightforward. Simply by including `packs-rails` in your `Gemfile` in **all environments**, `packs-rails` will automatically hook into and configure Rails.

From there, you can create a `./packs` folder and structure it using the conventions listed above.

If you wish to use a different directory name, eg `components` instead of `packs`, you can customize this by configuring `packs.yml`. See [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) for more information.

If you want to have your packs code namespaced without adding a directory with the pack's name into the directory structure, you can use the [automatic namespaces gem](https://github.com/gap777/automatic_namespaces).

## Modify spring to detect pack moves

If you use spring, when you move a pack, you'll want spring to update its cache

Add this to one of your initializers
```ruby
Packs::Specification::Configuration.fetch.pack_paths.each do |dir|
  Dir["#{dir}/package.yml"].each do |package_yml|
    Spring.watch(package_yml)
  end
end
```

### Splitting routes
`packs-rails` allows you to split your application routes for every pack. You just have to create a file describing your routes and then `draw` them in your root `config/routes.rb` file (NOTE: the `draw` function is only in Rails 6.1+).

# packwerk-extensions

`packwerk-extensions` is a home for checker extensions for [packwerk](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk) 3.

Currently, it ships the following checkers to help improve the boundaries between packages. These checkers are:
- A `privacy` checker that ensures other packages are using your package's public API
- A `visibility` checker that allows packages to be private except to an explicit group of other packages.
- A `folder_privacy` checker that allows packages to their sibling packs and parent pack (to be used in an application that uses folder packs)
- A `layer` (formerly `architecture`) checker that allows packages to specify their "layer" and requires that each layer only communicate with layers below it.

## Installation

Add `packwerk-extensions` to your `Gemfile`.

To register all checkers included in this gem, add the following to your `packwerk.yml`:

```yaml
require:
  - packwerk-extensions
```

Alternatively, you can require individual checkers:

```yaml
require:
  - packwerk/privacy/checker
  - packwerk/visibility/checker
  - packwerk/folder_privacy/checker
  - packwerk/layer/checker
```

## Privacy Checker
The privacy checker extension was originally extracted from [packwerk](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk).

A package's privacy boundary is violated when there is a reference to the package's private constants from a source outside the package.

To enforce privacy for your package, set `enforce_privacy` to `true` or `strict` on your pack:

```yaml
# components/merchandising/package.yml
enforce_privacy: true
```

Setting `enforce_privacy` to `true` will make all references to private constants in your package a violation.

Setting `enforce_privacy` to `strict` will forbid all references to private constants in your package. **This includes violations that have been added to other packages' `package_todo.yml` files.**

Note: You will need to remove all existing privacy violations before setting `enforce_privacy` to `strict`.

### Using public folders
You may enforce privacy either way mentioned above and still expose a public API for your package by placing constants in the public folder, which by default is `app/public`. The constants in the public folder will be made available for use by the rest of the application.

### Defining your own public folder

You may prefer to override the default public folder, you can do so on a per-package basis by defining a `public_path`.

Example:

```yaml
public_path: my/custom/path/
```

### Defining public constants through sigil

> [!WARNING]
> This way of of defining the public API of a package should be considered WIP. It is not supported by all tooling in the RubyAtScale ecosystem, as @alexevanczuk pointed out in a [comment on the PR](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packwerk-extensions/pull/35#discussion_r1334331797):
>
> There are a couple of other places that will require changes related to this sigil. Namely, everything that is coupled to the public folder implementation of privacy.
>
> In the rubyatscale org:
>
> * pack_stats, example https://github.com/rubyatscale/pack_stats/blob/main/lib/pack_stats/private/metrics/public_usage.rb. (IMO though we can just remove this metric – it has never been useful)
> * Other places that mention public_path or app/public.
>   * Org wide search for app/public link
>   * Org wide search for public_path link
>   * packs (the Rust port of packwerk – I could take this one over unless someone is interested in implementing whatever we come up with there



You may make individual files public within a private package by usage of a comment within the first 5 lines of the `.rb` file containing `pack_public: true`.

A package's dependency boundary is violated whenever it references a constant in some package that has not been declared as a dependency.

Specify `enforce_dependencies: true` to start enforcing the dependencies of a package. The intentional dependencies of the package are specified as a list under a `dependencies:` key.

Example:

```yaml
# components/shop_identity/package.yml
enforce_dependencies: true
dependencies:
  - components/platform
```

It will be a dependency violation when `components/shop_identity` tries to reference a constant that is not within `components/platform` or itself.

#### Using strict mode

Once there are no more violations in a package, you can turn on `strict` mode, which will prevent new violations from being added to the package's `package_todo.yml`. To use this, simply change `enforce_dependencies: true` to `enforce_dependencies: strict` in your `package.yml`.

Then, when you run `bin/packwerk check`, new violations will cause the following error to be displayed:
```
packs/referencing_package cannot have dependency violations on packs/defining_package because strict mode is enabled for dependency violations in packs/referencing_package/package.yml
```

Once the `strict` mode is enabled on a package, running `bin/packwerk update-todo` will not add new violations in the package_todo.yml file and the command will return an error.

## Checking for violations

After enforcing the boundary checks for a package, you may execute:

    bin/packwerk check

Packwerk will check the entire codebase for any new or stale violations.

You can also specify folders for a shorter run time. When checking against folders all subfolders will be analyzed, irrespective of nested package boundaries.

    bin/packwerk check components/your_package

You can also specify packages for a shorter run time. When checking against packages any packages nested underneath the specified packages will not be checked. This can be helpful to test packages like the root package, which can have many nested packages.

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def initialize(catalog: Catalog)
      @catalog = catalog
    end

    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      tenant_id = payload.fetch('tenant_id')
      document_id = payload.fetch('id')
      snapshot = @catalog.list(tenant_id: tenant_id).find { |row| row.fetch('id') == document_id }
      raise 'unpublished document' unless snapshot

      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: snapshot)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: snapshot }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      PublishedDocumentQuery.all_published
    end
  end
end

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

    self.table_name = 'deliveries'
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class Embedding < ActiveRecord::Base
    self.table_name = 'embeddings'
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class Catalog
    def self.list(tenant_id:)
      Document.where(tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

# Package operations with upstream packs

Use this reference when creating, exposing, moving or inspecting a context. Foundry is built on Rails, packs, packs-rails and Packwerk. `packs-specification` discovers topology; `packs` changes packages; `packs-rails` supplies Rails integration; Packwerk/extensions own dependency, privacy and cycle checks. Foundry adds architectural intent and guidance.

## Prepare the consuming application

Read its Gemfile.lock, packs.yml, packwerk.yml, package.yml, adjacent foundry.yml files and workflow selection. Work from that application root. Keep packs-rails in every environment; keep Foundry and analysis tools in development/test. Commands below target packs 0.3.0; inspect the locked CLI before using another version.

```sh
bundle exec packs help
bundle exec packs help create
```

`bundle binstubs packwerk` creates bin/packwerk, required by upstream validation and dependency-edit commands. An optional `bundle binstubs packs` creates bin/packs. Review existing binstubs before generation; do not force replacement. Upstream `packs check` and `packs validate` invoke bin/packwerk (or pks if explicitly configured). Without binstubs, use `bundle exec packwerk check` and `bundle exec packwerk validate` directly. Keep Packwerk authoritative; enabling pks requires application-specific parity evidence.

## Create and constrain a context

Create a plain package with explicit enforcement choices:

```sh
bundle exec packs create packs/billing --enforce-dependencies --enforce-privacy --no-enforce-layers
```

Before creation, ensure packwerk.yml loads packwerk-extensions for privacy checking. Review upstream output and add an adjacent packs/billing/foundry.yml:

```yaml
schema: 1
namespace: Billing
profile: rails_native
patterns:
  events: none
  cqrs: none
capabilities: {}
```

The package.yml owns dependencies/public paths/stewardship; foundry.yml owns architecture. A plain upstream pack does not receive Foundry intent automatically. Existing packs without a sidecar remain valid for incremental adoption. The optional `bin/rails generate foundry:context billing --profile=rails_native --pretend` previews a combined scaffold; remove --pretend only when that scaffold is wanted. Neither route implements a feature.

## Dependencies and public APIs

```sh
bundle exec packs add_dependency packs/billing packs/customers
bundle exec packs get_info packs/billing
bundle exec packs list_top_violations privacy packs/customers --limit=10
```

add_dependency mutates and normalizes the source package.yml and then runs bin/packwerk validate. Preflight that binstub and use an isolated Rails environment; a validation failure can leave the dependency edit in place. It permits a dependency, not private access. Expose a narrow public API under the destination package's actual public_path (normally app/public), and keep private Active Record objects inside their owner. Same-pack controllers/jobs can use internal objects. Violation summaries read accepted debt; they are not fresh source analysis.

Feature controllers, views, jobs, channels, mailers, agents, tools and schemas stay in the pack. Rails base classes and shared delivery stay in the shell; migrations stay at root. Use explicit namespaces and ordinary autoload roots: app/models/billing/invoice.rb defines Billing::Invoice. A pack can own config/routes/billing.rb; draw :billing from root config/routes.rb. Keep tests in the pack and pass their paths explicitly to Rails test commands.

## Custom roots and moves

Honor pack_paths in packs.yml, including nested configured roots; do not infer ownership solely from the packs/ prefix. Create at the intended upstream path and use that exact path for dependencies. For optional Foundry scaffolding, supply --path=components/billing. Nested directories do not establish Ruby namespaces automatically.

`packs make_public PATH` moves code to the public path. `packs move DESTINATION_PACK PATH` moves code between owners. `packs rename` is interactive in 0.3.0; it does not take invented old/new positional arguments. `move_to_parent CHILD PARENT` and `move_to_folder PACK DIRECTORY` change topology. These commands can rewrite source, metadata and debt through upstream post-processors. Use them in a reviewed branch with a clean baseline and inspect every change.

After a move, review Ruby namespaces, references, routes, tests, public paths, foundry.yml, prompt lookup and .foundry receipts. Packs does not reconcile Foundry receipts. Do not edit hashes to make a generator accept moved code. Preserve the original receipt as provenance; explicitly relocate/reconcile owned artifacts with a disposable fresh scaffold when necessary. Verify fresh-process Rails loading and behavior before accepting the move.

## Checks and debt

```sh
bundle exec foundry check --sources
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec packwerk validate
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec packwerk check
bin/rails zeitwerk:check
bin/rails test packs/billing/test
```

Full Packwerk checks can boot Rails; use an isolated environment/database. `foundry check --boundaries` also verifies accepted debt bytes stay unchanged. Record behavioral tests separately from static evidence. Do not run `packs update` (update-todo) during normal no-new-debt checks. `packs lint_package_todo_yml_files` also invokes debt regeneration in 0.3.0, despite its name. Review formatting/move operations for writes; never silently accept regenerated debt. Use Foundry audit in a disposable copy to propose resolved-debt cleanup.

Upstream references: [packs](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs), [packs-rails](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs-rails).

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

# Independently useful adoption checkpoints

Use this reference for an existing application or an explicit context refactor. Adapt the
checkpoints to the authorized change; do not require advanced persistence, events or AI
just because a worked example uses them.

Before editing, identify the selected workflow, actual package roots, owning tables,
public callers and accepted debt. Run `foundry adopt --format=json` for read-only context;
its recommendations are starting points, not proof that migration occurred. For a configured
context, `foundry plan refactor --context=NAME` adds selected-context source evidence.
`complete: true` means the assessment finished. It does not mean a migration is implemented.

| Checkpoint | Evidence before proceeding | Rollback boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characterization | Endpoints, authorization, tenant isolation, persisted records, failed writes and externally visible errors | No application changes yet |
| Package extraction | Same behavioral tests, ordinary Rails loading, existing table/model identity, declared package dependencies | Move code/configuration back using a recorded patch; retain the unchanged database |
| Public caller repair | An intentional private access fails Packwerk before repair; repaired callers pass; reviewed debt identities are resolved | Restore the prior caller/public API checkpoint; do not silently broaden privacy |
| Separate persistence change | Existing IDs, revisions, ownership, transaction rollback and failure behavior remain equivalent | State whether previous code still understands all written data; take an appropriate backup before irreversible data changes |
| Subsequent features | Integration crash/retry tests, rebuild/tenant/provider evidence relevant to the requested feature | Describe how to disable delivery and recover pending work without losing authoritative state |

For extraction, retain Active Record and current tables unless changing persistence is itself
the authorized task. Establish a useful business boundary first. Keep controllers/views/jobs
with their feature, shared bases in the shell, migrations at root and loading delegated to
packs-rails. Reconcile namespaces and receipts explicitly; preserve custom roots.

Record the starting revision, commands, actual outcomes, files/data changed and rollback
instructions for each checkpoint. Run normal Packwerk checks against unchanged accepted
baselines. Use `foundry audit` in a disposable environment to review new/retained/resolved
identities; edit accepted debt only after that review, never as an automatic way to make
checks pass. A failed checkpoint remains unfinished until repaired or rolled back.

Use the application's selected workflow to record behavior and decisions; keep established
history. With workflow none, a plain checkpoint record and executable tests are sufficient.
Keep application configuration authoritative rather than copying a second dependency graph
into the plan. Report structural, boundary, behavioral and workflow results separately.

# Native context conventions

For a new application, `foundry new NAME` delegates to Rails and defaults to Spec Kit. Explicit `--specs=openspec|none` is supported. Foundry belongs to development/test; application execution uses packs-rails, Dry::Operation and Rails directly. The default stack is PostgreSQL, Puma, Hotwire and Solid Queue, without an additional cache service. Inspect interrupted creation before retrying; the command never merges into an existing destination.

Read the owning `package.yml` and adjacent `foundry.yml`. Profiles are `rails_native`, `modular`, and `domain`. Event and CQRS patterns are independent. Capability selections never silently promote a profile. Use the consuming application's existing package roots; new contexts default to `packs/`.

Use direct upstream packs commands for package operations; read [pack operations](packs.md). Optional `foundry:context NAME --profile=PROFILE` and component generators with `--context=NAME` offer small scaffolds. Native command, query, model, operation, entity, value-object, policy, port, and repository placement follows the selected profile. Migrations remain in the Rails application root. Introduce repositories and ports for an actual boundary; efficient Active Record reads remain valid in every profile.

Domain commands under `app/application/billing/commands/` define `Billing::Commands::*`. Modular commands under `app/commands/billing/` define `Billing::*`. Models inherit the host's `ApplicationRecord`. Native operations inherit `Dry::Operation`, use `skip_prepending`, and establish one `steps`/`step` result boundary. Transactional commands inspect the failed result inside the transaction and raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback`. The generated savepoint prevents nested failed writes from leaking. Application callers decide whether a failed inner command also aborts their larger transaction.

Feature-owned delivery stays in the pack; Rails base classes and shared delivery stay in the shell. Same-pack delivery can call internal application objects. Cross-pack callers use declared dependencies and public contracts. Upstream `packs-rails` provides Rails loading. Foundry has no application loader.

For AI, select `capabilities.ai.adapter: ruby_llm` explicitly and add optional RubyLLM `~> 1.16.0` to the application bundle. Optional `foundry:agent NAME --context=NAME` creates direct RubyLLM agents/tools/schemas and plain `app/prompts` instructions inside the owning pack, a behavioral contract and an evaluation starting case. Fill the application-owned `config/ai.yml` model aliases and pass a selected alias's model/provider options to the agent constructor, together with `operation:` and `authorize:` callables. Authorization must bind a trusted principal and run before each tool execution; the operation enforces tenant scope. Generated instructions use `File.read(File.expand_path(..., __dir__))`, avoiding ERB evaluation of injected Proc inputs and working-directory assumptions. Keep user/tool content in its message role, validate structured output in application code, and add offline workflow tests. Explicit `foundry check --prompts` verifies declarations and files; it does not execute evaluations or establish model quality.

Replace scaffold exceptions with meaningful behavior and tests. Keep normal tests offline and external requests outside database transactions. Use constructor injection. Do not introduce a Foundry container, event bus, aggregate engine, projection runtime, AI execution store, or specification-provider abstraction.

Use `foundry plan refactor --context=NAME --profile=PROFILE` for a read-only assessment. Its detected references are source evidence, not proof of runtime reachability, a data conversion, or a completed migration.

Read root `config/foundry.yml` before generation: its defaults apply to new contexts unless explicitly overridden. `foundry:context` accepts independent `--events` and `--cqrs` selections; selecting a pattern records intent and does not install a capability implementation. Workload never changes another axis automatically.

Start native adoption with `foundry adopt --format=json`. It preserves established workflow selection, existing roots, specifications and accepted Packwerk debt. `foundry check` validates configuration and namespace ownership without Rails boot. Explicit `foundry check --boundaries` runs upstream Packwerk validate/check in the locked consumer bundle and test environment; use an isolated test application because initializers may execute. It preserves accepted debt files, propagates upstream failures and never regenerates baselines. Review fully resolved baselines separately: Packwerk 3.1.0 can miss those stale entries. Run behavioral tests separately, and do not claim pks parity or complete debt cleanup from this check.

Optional ROM writes must persist business state and outbox intent through the same ROM gateway transaction, with explicit rollback of failed native results. Deliver to RES or another destination after commit with stable IDs and idempotent recovery. dry-system is optional wiring and Trailblazer an alternative native workflow; neither warrants a Foundry container or result wrapper.

For Foundry 1.x tooling upgrades, inspect `foundry --version` and `foundry contracts` before interpreting configuration or JSON evidence. Reports identify report_schema, foundry_version and report_kind; reject unsupported schemas and ignore additive fields. Read success/complete and the declared limitations, not completion prose. Root schema 1 rejects unknown fields; checks/adoption currently have no policy keys. Use explicit CLI checks instead of inventing configuration switches.

A gem update does not rewrite application code or installed skills. Preserve receipts and local edits. Compare fresh output in a disposable destination, then apply reviewed changes with behavioral tests. An old skill receipt requires manual catalog review; do not edit its hashes to bypass a conflict. Preserve workflow history and accepted debt, and regenerate old parity evidence against the current inputs. The installed gem's docs/stable-contracts.md describes compatibility and recovery policy.

## Delivery and evidence

Native generation uses `--context=NAME` with ordinary Rails loading. Delivery entrypoints include `foundry:controller`, `foundry:job`, `foundry:mailer`, and `foundry:channel`; they generate classes inside the owning pack and inherit application shell base classes. For example, `bin/rails generate foundry:controller invoices --context=billing` defines `Billing::InvoicesController`. Add routes, views, actions and behavioral tests with ordinary Rails conventions.

The generator creates `Support::SummarizeAgent`, `Support::SummarizeTool` and `Support::SummarizeSchema` under the pack's `app/agents`, `app/tools` and `app/schemas`. Delivery placement is the same in all profiles. It also creates `packs/support/app/prompts/support/summarize_agent/instructions.txt`, `contract.yml` and `evaluation.yml` inside the owning pack, pack-owned authorization tests, and a generation receipt. Names derive from the configured context namespace, including nested namespaces and existing package roots.

## Characterization (pre-change)

- `/documents` returns published documents for the tenant implied by `Authorization` header tokens.
- `Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id:)` returns `id`, `tenant_id`, `body`, `revision` ordered by `id`.
- Persistence uses the root `documents`, `embeddings`, and `deliveries` tables unchanged.

## Package extraction

Moved Knowledge models and services under `packs/knowledge`. Public API: `packs/knowledge/app/public/knowledge/catalog.rb`.

## Rollback

Revert the commit that introduced `packs/knowledge` and restore files under `app/models/knowledge` and `app/services/knowledge`. No database migration was applied; SQLite test schema is unchanged.

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

  end

  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      snapshot_revision = snapshot.revision
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

        result = :stored
      end
      result
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def job
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new
  end

  def test_discarded_when_not_published
    doc = document(published: false)
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_document_deleted_during_provider
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.delete(doc.id)
      [1.0]
    end
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_revision_changes_during_provider
    doc = document(revision: 1)
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(revision: 2)
      [1.0]
    end
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_unpublished_during_provider
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(published: false)
      [1.0]
    end
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_tenant_changes_during_provider
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(tenant_id: 'b')
      [1.0]
    end
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: provider)
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_does_not_overwrite_newer_embedding_with_older_result
    doc = document(revision: 2)
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(
      document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', revision: 3, version: 'v1', vector: '[0.9]'
    )
    result = job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [0.1] })
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal '[0.9]', Knowledge::Embedding.find_by(document_id: doc.id, version: 'v1').vector
  end

  def test_different_embedding_versions_coexist
    doc = document
    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_b) { [1] })
    assert_equal :stored, job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v2', provider: ->(_b) { [2] })
    assert_equal 2, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_provider_error_propagates_without_writing
    doc = document
    assert_raises(RuntimeError) do
      job.call(document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { raise 'provider failed' })
    end
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end
end

      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end

# packs-rails

`packs-rails` establishes and implements a set of conventions for splitting up large monoliths built on top of the [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) standard. `packs-rails` makes it easy to use [`packwerk`](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk) to modularize your rails app. With `packs-rails`, new packages' autoload paths are automatically added to Rails, so your code will immediately become usable and loadable without additional configuration.

Here is an example application that uses `packs-rails`:
```
package.yml # root level pack
app/ # Unpackaged code
  models/
  ...
packs/
  my_domain/
    package.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    package_todo.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    app/
      public/ # Recommended location for public API
        my_domain.rb # creates the primary namespaces
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain.rb
      services/ # Private services
        my_domain/
          some_private_class.rb
      models/ # Private models
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model.rb # this works too
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model.rb
      controllers/
      views/
    config/
      initializers/ # Initializers can live in packs and load as expected
    lib/
      tasks/
    spec/ # With packs-rails, specs for a pack live next to the pack
      public/
        my_domain_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain_spec.rb
      services/
        my_domain/
          some_private_class_spec.rb
      models/
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_spec.rb
      factories/ # packs-rails will automatically load pack factories into FactoryBot, see Ecosystem and Integrations#factory_bot below
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
  my_other_domain/
    ... # other packs have a similar structure
  my_other_other_domain/
    ...
```

## Usage

Setting up `packs-rails` is straightforward. Simply by including `packs-rails` in your `Gemfile` in **all environments**, `packs-rails` will automatically hook into and configure Rails.

From there, you can create a `./packs` folder and structure it using the conventions listed above.

If you wish to use a different directory name, eg `components` instead of `packs`, you can customize this by configuring `packs.yml`. See [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) for more information.

If you want to have your packs code namespaced without adding a directory with the pack's name into the directory structure, you can use the [automatic namespaces gem](https://github.com/gap777/automatic_namespaces).

## Modify spring to detect pack moves

If you use spring, when you move a pack, you'll want spring to update its cache

Add this to one of your initializers
```ruby
Packs::Specification::Configuration.fetch.pack_paths.each do |dir|
  Dir["#{dir}/package.yml"].each do |package_yml|
    Spring.watch(package_yml)
  end
end
```

### Splitting routes
`packs-rails` allows you to split your application routes for every pack. You just have to create a file describing your routes and then `draw` them in your root `config/routes.rb` file (NOTE: the `draw` function is only in Rails 6.1+).

```ruby
# packs/my_domain/config/routes/my_domain.rb
resources :my_resource

# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  draw(:my_domain)
end
```

## Ecosystem and Integrations

### RSpec Integration
Simply add `--require packs/rails/rspec` to your `.rspec`.
Or, if you'd like, pass it as an argument to `rspec`:

```
$ rspec --require packs/rails/rspec ...
```

Integration will allow you to run tests as such:
```
# Run all specs in your entire application (packs and all):
rspec

# Run just that one test:
rspec spec/some/specific_spec.rb

# Run all tests under the "foobar" pack and all the tests of its nested packs:
rspec packs/foobar

# Same as above but also adds the "binbaz" pack:
rspec packs/foobar pack/binbaz

# Run all test files inside the "packs/foobar/spec" directory:
rspec packs/foobar/spec

# Run all specs under the "packs/foobar/nested_pack" pack:
rspec packs/foobar/nested_pack
```

#### factory_bot and factory_bot_rails

Ensure you have the gem in your Gemfile, and that `require: false` is not present, otherwise the `packs-rails` FactoryBot integration will not be run upon application/environment load.
This integration will automatically add the `[spec|test]/factories` directory from each pack to the application's `config.factory_bot.definition_file_paths`.

Using the example application above:
```
...
packs/
  my_domain/
    ...
    spec/ # OR test/
      ...
      factories/
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
  my_other_domain/
    ...
    spec/ # OR test/
      ...
      factories/
        my_other_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
```

#### rubocop-rails
[rubocop-rails](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop-rails) [targets paths](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop-rails/blob/master/config/default.yml) starting with `app/`. You might need to override the `Include` globs to include your packs code.

Examples:
```yml
Rails/EnumHash:
  Include:
    - '**/app/models/**/*.rb'
Rails/InverseOf:
  Include:
    - '**/app/models/**/*.rb'
Rails/LexicallyScopedActionFilter:
  Include:
    - '**/app/controllers/**/*.rb'
    - '**/app/mailers/**/*.rb'
```

#### parallel_tests

`parallel_tests` has it its own spec discovery mechanism, so packs-rails's RSpec integration doesn't do anything when you use them together.
To make them work, you'll need to explicitly specify the spec paths:

```bash
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec parallel_test spec packs/**/spec -t rspec <other_options>
```

#### Knapsack (Pro)

Similarly, Knapsack (and its Pro version) has its own spec discovery mechanism and the API will find and queue the relevant specs.
To make it discover your pack tests as well, you'll need to configure the following variables:

```yaml
KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_DIR: spec
KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_FILE_PATTERN: '{spec,packs}/**{,/*/**}/*_spec.rb'
```

Setting `KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_FILE_PATTERN` will tell Knapsack where your specs are located, while setting `KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_DIR` is necessary because otherwise an incorrect value is sent to rspec via the `--default-path` option.

## Contributing

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub at https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs-rails.

# Packwerk [![Build Status](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/workflows/CI/badge.svg)](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/actions?query=workflow%3ACI)

> "I know who you are and because of that I know what you do."
> This knowledge is a dependency that raises the cost of change.

-- _Sandi Metz, Practical Object-Oriented Design in Ruby_

Packwerk is a Ruby gem used to enforce boundaries and modularize Rails applications.

Packwerk can be used to:
* Combine groups of files into packages
* Define package-level constant visibility (i.e. have publicly accessible constants)
* Help existing codebases to become more modular without obstructing development

## Prerequisites

Packwerk needs [Zeitwerk](https://github.com/fxn/zeitwerk) enabled, which comes with Rails 6.

Packwerk supports MRI versions 2.7 and above.

## Demo

Watch a [1-minute video demo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NwqlyBAxVpQ&feature=youtu.be) on how Packwerk works.

[![](./static/packwerk-check-demo.png)](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NwqlyBAxVpQ&feature=youtu.be)

## Installation

1. Add this line to your application's Gemfile:

```ruby
gem 'packwerk'
```

2. Install the gem

Execute:

    $ bundle install

Or install it yourself as:

    $ gem install packwerk

2. Run `bundle binstub packwerk` to generate the binstub
3. Run `bin/packwerk init` to generate the configuration files

## Usage

Read [USAGE.md](USAGE.md) for usage once Packwerk is installed on your project.

## Pronunciation

"Packwerk" is pronounced [[ˈpakvɛʁk]](https://cdn.shopify.com/s/files/1/0258/7469/files/packwerk.mp3).

## Ecosystem

Various third parties have built tooling on top of packwerk. Here's a selection of some that might prove useful:

- https://github.com/bellroy/graphwerk draws a graph of your package dependencies
- https://github.com/rubyatscale/packwerk-vscode integrates packwerk into Visual Studio Code so you can see violations right in your editor
- https://github.com/vinted/packwerk-intellij integrates packwerk into RubyMine so you can see violations right in your editor
- https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs-rails sets up Rails autoloading, as well as `rspec` and `FactoryBot` integration, for packages arranged in a flat list. packs-rails is quite convenient, but for autoloading we recommend to use `Rails::Engine`s instead.
- https://github.com/rubyatscale/danger-packwerk integrates packwerk with [danger.systems](https://danger.systems) to provide packwerk feedback as Github inline PR comments
- https://github.com/rubyatscale/packwerk-extensions contains extensions for packwerk, including a checker for packwerk that allows you to enforce public API boundaries. This was originally extracted from `packwerk` itself.
- https://github.com/alexevanczuk/packs is a Rust implementation of packwerk that has experimental support for non-Rails, non-Zeitwerk applications.

## Development

After checking out the repo, run `bin/setup` to install dependencies. Then, run `rake test` to run the tests. You can also run `bin/console` for an interactive prompt that will allow you to experiment.

## Limitations

With Ruby being a very dynamic language, static analysis tools such as Packwerk are bound to have limitations.
To reduce the impact of those limitations, Packwerk is designed to avoid false positives (reporting references as violations that are actually fine) at any cost, and we pay the cost by accepting a small number of false negatives (failing to report actual violations).

- Packwerk can only resolve references to constants that are defined in code loaded by the application's Zeitwerk autoloader.
  This is because we rely on [Zeitwerk's conventions](https://github.com/fxn/zeitwerk#file-structure), and code that is loaded differently (like through an explicit `require`) often doesn't follow these conventions.
- Method calls and objects passed around the application are completely ignored. Packwerk only cares about static constant references. That said, if you want Packwerk to analyze parameters of a method, you can use [Sorbet](https://sorbet.org/) to define a type signature. Sorbet signatures are pure Ruby code and use constants to express types, and Packwerk understands that.
- Support for custom Zeitwerk configuration is limited. If [custom ActiveSupport inflections](https://guides.rubyonrails.org/autoloading_and_reloading_constants.html#customizing-inflections) are used, Packwerk will understand that and everything is fine. However, if Zeitwerk is directly configured with [custom Zeitwerk inflections](https://github.com/fxn/zeitwerk#inflection) or to [collapse directories](https://github.com/fxn/zeitwerk#collapsing-directories), _Packwerk will get confused and produce false positives_.

Read and follow the guidelines in [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

# packwerk-extensions

`packwerk-extensions` is a home for checker extensions for [packwerk](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk) 3.

Currently, it ships the following checkers to help improve the boundaries between packages. These checkers are:
- A `privacy` checker that ensures other packages are using your package's public API
- A `visibility` checker that allows packages to be private except to an explicit group of other packages.
- A `folder_privacy` checker that allows packages to their sibling packs and parent pack (to be used in an application that uses folder packs)
- A `layer` (formerly `architecture`) checker that allows packages to specify their "layer" and requires that each layer only communicate with layers below it.

## Installation

Add `packwerk-extensions` to your `Gemfile`.

To register all checkers included in this gem, add the following to your `packwerk.yml`:

```yaml
require:
  - packwerk-extensions
```

Alternatively, you can require individual checkers:

```yaml
require:
  - packwerk/privacy/checker
  - packwerk/visibility/checker
  - packwerk/folder_privacy/checker
  - packwerk/layer/checker
```

## Privacy Checker
The privacy checker extension was originally extracted from [packwerk](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk).

A package's privacy boundary is violated when there is a reference to the package's private constants from a source outside the package.

To enforce privacy for your package, set `enforce_privacy` to `true` or `strict` on your pack:

```yaml
# components/merchandising/package.yml
enforce_privacy: true
```

Setting `enforce_privacy` to `true` will make all references to private constants in your package a violation.

Setting `enforce_privacy` to `strict` will forbid all references to private constants in your package. **This includes violations that have been added to other packages' `package_todo.yml` files.**

Note: You will need to remove all existing privacy violations before setting `enforce_privacy` to `strict`.

### Using public folders
You may enforce privacy either way mentioned above and still expose a public API for your package by placing constants in the public folder, which by default is `app/public`. The constants in the public folder will be made available for use by the rest of the application.

### Defining your own public folder

You may prefer to override the default public folder, you can do so on a per-package basis by defining a `public_path`.

Example:

```yaml
public_path: my/custom/path/
```

### Defining public constants through sigil

> [!WARNING]
> This way of of defining the public API of a package should be considered WIP. It is not supported by all tooling in the RubyAtScale ecosystem, as @alexevanczuk pointed out in a [comment on the PR](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packwerk-extensions/pull/35#discussion_r1334331797):
>

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error

        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }

      delivery.update!(delivered: true)

    end

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

    def documents
      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

# Native context conventions

For a new application, `foundry new NAME` delegates to Rails and defaults to Spec Kit. Explicit `--specs=openspec|none` is supported. Foundry belongs to development/test; application execution uses packs-rails, Dry::Operation and Rails directly. The default stack is PostgreSQL, Puma, Hotwire and Solid Queue, without an additional cache service. Inspect interrupted creation before retrying; the command never merges into an existing destination.

Read the owning `package.yml` and adjacent `foundry.yml`. Profiles are `rails_native`, `modular`, and `domain`. Event and CQRS patterns are independent. Capability selections never silently promote a profile. Use the consuming application's existing package roots; new contexts default to `packs/`.

Use direct upstream packs commands for package operations; read [pack operations](packs.md). Optional `foundry:context NAME --profile=PROFILE` and component generators with `--context=NAME` offer small scaffolds. Native command, query, model, operation, entity, value-object, policy, port, and repository placement follows the selected profile. Migrations remain in the Rails application root. Introduce repositories and ports for an actual boundary; efficient Active Record reads remain valid in every profile.

Domain commands under `app/application/billing/commands/` define `Billing::Commands::*`. Modular commands under `app/commands/billing/` define `Billing::*`. Models inherit the host's `ApplicationRecord`. Native operations inherit `Dry::Operation`, use `skip_prepending`, and establish one `steps`/`step` result boundary. Transactional commands inspect the failed result inside the transaction and raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback`. The generated savepoint prevents nested failed writes from leaking. Application callers decide whether a failed inner command also aborts their larger transaction.

Feature-owned delivery stays in the pack; Rails base classes and shared delivery stay in the shell. Same-pack delivery can call internal application objects. Cross-pack callers use declared dependencies and public contracts. Upstream `packs-rails` provides Rails loading. Foundry has no application loader.

For AI, select `capabilities.ai.adapter: ruby_llm` explicitly and add optional RubyLLM `~> 1.16.0` to the application bundle. Optional `foundry:agent NAME --context=NAME` creates direct RubyLLM agents/tools/schemas and plain `app/prompts` instructions inside the owning pack, a behavioral contract and an evaluation starting case. Fill the application-owned `config/ai.yml` model aliases and pass a selected alias's model/provider options to the agent constructor, together with `operation:` and `authorize:` callables. Authorization must bind a trusted principal and run before each tool execution; the operation enforces tenant scope. Generated instructions use `File.read(File.expand_path(..., __dir__))`, avoiding ERB evaluation of injected Proc inputs and working-directory assumptions. Keep user/tool content in its message role, validate structured output in application code, and add offline workflow tests. Explicit `foundry check --prompts` verifies declarations and files; it does not execute evaluations or establish model quality.

Replace scaffold exceptions with meaningful behavior and tests. Keep normal tests offline and external requests outside database transactions. Use constructor injection. Do not introduce a Foundry container, event bus, aggregate engine, projection runtime, AI execution store, or specification-provider abstraction.

Use `foundry plan refactor --context=NAME --profile=PROFILE` for a read-only assessment. Its detected references are source evidence, not proof of runtime reachability, a data conversion, or a completed migration.

Read root `config/foundry.yml` before generation: its defaults apply to new contexts unless explicitly overridden. `foundry:context` accepts independent `--events` and `--cqrs` selections; selecting a pattern records intent and does not install a capability implementation. Workload never changes another axis automatically.

Start native adoption with `foundry adopt --format=json`. It preserves established workflow selection, existing roots, specifications and accepted Packwerk debt. `foundry check` validates configuration and namespace ownership without Rails boot. Explicit `foundry check --boundaries` runs upstream Packwerk validate/check in the locked consumer bundle and test environment; use an isolated test application because initializers may execute. It preserves accepted debt files, propagates upstream failures and never regenerates baselines. Review fully resolved baselines separately: Packwerk 3.1.0 can miss those stale entries. Run behavioral tests separately, and do not claim pks parity or complete debt cleanup from this check.

Optional ROM writes must persist business state and outbox intent through the same ROM gateway transaction, with explicit rollback of failed native results. Deliver to RES or another destination after commit with stable IDs and idempotent recovery. dry-system is optional wiring and Trailblazer an alternative native workflow; neither warrants a Foundry container or result wrapper.

For Foundry 1.x tooling upgrades, inspect `foundry --version` and `foundry contracts` before interpreting configuration or JSON evidence. Reports identify report_schema, foundry_version and report_kind; reject unsupported schemas and ignore additive fields. Read success/complete and the declared limitations, not completion prose. Root schema 1 rejects unknown fields; checks/adoption currently have no policy keys. Use explicit CLI checks instead of inventing configuration switches.

A gem update does not rewrite application code or installed skills. Preserve receipts and local edits. Compare fresh output in a disposable destination, then apply reviewed changes with behavioral tests. An old skill receipt requires manual catalog review; do not edit its hashes to bypass a conflict. Preserve workflow history and accepted debt, and regenerate old parity evidence against the current inputs. The installed gem's docs/stable-contracts.md describes compatibility and recovery policy.

# Independently useful adoption checkpoints

Use this reference for an existing application or an explicit context refactor. Adapt the
checkpoints to the authorized change; do not require advanced persistence, events or AI
just because a worked example uses them.

Before editing, identify the selected workflow, actual package roots, owning tables,
public callers and accepted debt. Run `foundry adopt --format=json` for read-only context;
its recommendations are starting points, not proof that migration occurred. For a configured
context, `foundry plan refactor --context=NAME` adds selected-context source evidence.
`complete: true` means the assessment finished. It does not mean a migration is implemented.

| Checkpoint | Evidence before proceeding | Rollback boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characterization | Endpoints, authorization, tenant isolation, persisted records, failed writes and externally visible errors | No application changes yet |
| Package extraction | Same behavioral tests, ordinary Rails loading, existing table/model identity, declared package dependencies | Move code/configuration back using a recorded patch; retain the unchanged database |
| Public caller repair | An intentional private access fails Packwerk before repair; repaired callers pass; reviewed debt identities are resolved | Restore the prior caller/public API checkpoint; do not silently broaden privacy |
| Separate persistence change | Existing IDs, revisions, ownership, transaction rollback and failure behavior remain equivalent | State whether previous code still understands all written data; take an appropriate backup before irreversible data changes |
| Subsequent features | Integration crash/retry tests, rebuild/tenant/provider evidence relevant to the requested feature | Describe how to disable delivery and recover pending work without losing authoritative state |

For extraction, retain Active Record and current tables unless changing persistence is itself
the authorized task. Establish a useful business boundary first. Keep controllers/views/jobs
with their feature, shared bases in the shell, migrations at root and loading delegated to
packs-rails. Reconcile namespaces and receipts explicitly; preserve custom roots.

Record the starting revision, commands, actual outcomes, files/data changed and rollback
instructions for each checkpoint. Run normal Packwerk checks against unchanged accepted
baselines. Use `foundry audit` in a disposable environment to review new/retained/resolved
identities; edit accepted debt only after that review, never as an automatic way to make
checks pass. A failed checkpoint remains unfinished until repaired or rolled back.

Use the application's selected workflow to record behavior and decisions; keep established
history. With workflow none, a plain checkpoint record and executable tests are sufficient.
Keep application configuration authoritative rather than copying a second dependency graph
into the plan. Report structural, boundary, behavioral and workflow results separately.

require_relative 'test_helper'

class KnowledgeCatalogTest < BenchmarkTest
  def test_list_returns_published_documents_ordered_by_id
    second = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'second', revision: 1)
    first = Knowledge::Document.create!(tenant_id: 'a', body: 'first', revision: 1, published: true)
    document(tenant: 'b', body: 'other tenant')
    document(tenant: 'a', body: 'draft', published: false)

    rows = Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id: 'a')

    assert_equal [first.id, second.id], rows.map { |row| row.fetch('id') }
    rows.each do |row|
      assert_equal %w[id tenant_id body revision], row.keys.sort
      assert_equal 'a', row.fetch('tenant_id')
    end
  end

  def test_documents_delivery_uses_catalog_public_api
    expected = document
    get '/documents', {}, { 'HTTP_AUTHORIZATION' => 'tenant-a-token' }
    catalog_rows = Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id: 'a')

    assert_equal catalog_rows, JSON.parse(last_response.body)
    assert_equal [expected.id], catalog_rows.map { |row| row.fetch('id') }
  end
end

Knowledge models and services moved from `app/models/knowledge` and `app/services/knowledge` into `packs/knowledge`. `Knowledge::Catalog` is the public API at `packs/knowledge/app/public/knowledge/catalog.rb`. Root `package.yml` declares a dependency on `packs/knowledge`. The `documents` table and Active Record models are unchanged.

## Rollback (no database migration)

1. Move files from `packs/knowledge/app/models/knowledge`, `packs/knowledge/app/services/knowledge`, and `packs/knowledge/app/public/knowledge/catalog.rb` back to `app/models/knowledge`, `app/services/knowledge`, and `app/services/knowledge/catalog.rb` respectively.
2. Remove `packs/knowledge` and the `packs/knowledge` entry from root `package.yml` dependencies.
3. Restore `app/controllers/documents_controller.rb` to query `Knowledge::Document` directly if reverting the delivery boundary.
4. Run `bundle exec ruby -rstringio -S packwerk validate`, `bundle exec ruby -rstringio -S packwerk check`, and `bin/rails test`.

No persistence conversion was performed; rollback does not require data restore.

# Extract a knowledge boundary

Introduce a useful Knowledge business boundary without changing the existing /documents endpoint, tenant authentication, table or records. Expose Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id:) returning published document hashes ordered by id (id, tenant_id, body, revision). Delivery must call that API and must not access Knowledge::Document or persistence queries. Keep persistence internal to Knowledge. Existing public method signatures and unrelated jobs must continue working. For package-enabled applications move Knowledge-owned models/services/public API under packs/knowledge, configure enforced upstream privacy/dependencies and ordinary packs-rails loading; do not disable checks or add debt. Plain Rails uses the same API and behavior in ordinary Rails directories. Foundry applications additionally record the focal context as modular in its pack-local foundry.yml. Keep workflow none. Add characterization tests and document rollback before changing persistence; no persistence conversion is required.

Do not change dependency versions, visible tests, task instructions or disable verification. Add focused tests for your changes. Normal tests remain offline.

Use ordinary Rails and constructor injection. Workflow is none. Implement TASK.md, preserve public behavior, add focused tests, and run visible tests. Do not access external services or other workspaces.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class Catalog
    def self.list(tenant_id:)
      Document.where(tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

class DocumentsController < ActionController::Base
  def index
    tenant = { 'tenant-a-token' => 'a', 'tenant-b-token' => 'b' }[request.headers['Authorization']]
    return head :unauthorized unless tenant

    render json: Knowledge::Document.where(tenant_id: tenant, published: true).order(:id).map { |row| row.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision') }
  end
end

    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def initialize(catalog: Catalog)
      @catalog = catalog
    end

    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      data = published_payload(payload)
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: data)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: data }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end

    private

    def published_payload(payload)
      tenant_id = payload['tenant_id']
      return payload unless tenant_id

      rows = @catalog.list(tenant_id: tenant_id)
      rows.find { |row| row['id'] == payload['id'] } || payload
    end
  end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

# Reject stale embedding results

Knowledge::EmbeddingJob must avoid storing stale or unauthorized results. Read a tenant-scoped published snapshot, invoke provider.call(body) outside any database transaction, then recheck authoritative existence, tenant, publication state and revision before atomically storing an embedding for document/version. Return :discarded if initially unavailable or changed while the provider runs, otherwise :stored. A revision update, withdrawal, deletion or tenant reassignment during the provider call must leave no stale new embedding. Do not overwrite a newer embedding with an older result. Different embedding versions coexist. Provider errors propagate without writing. Keep public signatures and ordinary Rails execution.

Do not change dependency versions, visible tests, task instructions or disable verification. Add focused tests for your changes. Normal tests remain offline.

Use ordinary Rails and constructor injection. Workflow is none. Implement TASK.md, preserve public behavior, add focused tests, and run visible tests. Do not access external services or other workspaces.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
