# Package operations with upstream packs

Use this reference when creating, exposing, moving or inspecting a context. Foundry is built on Rails, packs, packs-rails and Packwerk. `packs-specification` discovers topology; `packs` changes packages; `packs-rails` supplies Rails integration; Packwerk/extensions own dependency, privacy and cycle checks. Foundry adds architectural intent and guidance.

## Prepare the consuming application

Read its Gemfile.lock, packs.yml, packwerk.yml, package.yml, adjacent foundry.yml files and workflow selection. Work from that application root. Keep packs-rails in every environment; keep Foundry and analysis tools in development/test. Commands below target packs 0.3.0; inspect the locked CLI before using another version.

```sh
bundle exec packs help
bundle exec packs help create
```

`bundle binstubs packwerk` creates bin/packwerk, required by upstream validation and dependency-edit commands. An optional `bundle binstubs packs` creates bin/packs. Review existing binstubs before generation; do not force replacement. Upstream `packs check` and `packs validate` invoke bin/packwerk (or pks if explicitly configured). Without binstubs, use `bundle exec packwerk check` and `bundle exec packwerk validate` directly. Keep Packwerk authoritative; enabling pks requires application-specific parity evidence.

## Create and constrain a context

Create a plain package with explicit enforcement choices:

```sh
bundle exec packs create packs/billing --enforce-dependencies --enforce-privacy --no-enforce-layers
```

Before creation, ensure packwerk.yml loads packwerk-extensions for privacy checking. Review upstream output and add an adjacent packs/billing/foundry.yml:

```yaml
schema: 1
namespace: Billing
profile: rails_native
patterns:
  events: none
  cqrs: none
capabilities: {}
```

The package.yml owns dependencies/public paths/stewardship; foundry.yml owns architecture. A plain upstream pack does not receive Foundry intent automatically. Existing packs without a sidecar remain valid for incremental adoption. The optional `bin/rails generate foundry:context billing --profile=rails_native --pretend` previews a combined scaffold; remove --pretend only when that scaffold is wanted. Neither route implements a feature.

## Dependencies and public APIs

```sh
bundle exec packs add_dependency packs/billing packs/customers
bundle exec packs get_info packs/billing
bundle exec packs list_top_violations privacy packs/customers --limit=10
```

add_dependency mutates and normalizes the source package.yml and then runs bin/packwerk validate. Preflight that binstub and use an isolated Rails environment; a validation failure can leave the dependency edit in place. It permits a dependency, not private access. Expose a narrow public API under the destination package's actual public_path (normally app/public), and keep private Active Record objects inside their owner. Same-pack controllers/jobs can use internal objects. Violation summaries read accepted debt; they are not fresh source analysis.

Feature controllers, views, jobs, channels, mailers, agents, tools and schemas stay in the pack. Rails base classes and shared delivery stay in the shell; migrations stay at root. Use explicit namespaces and ordinary autoload roots: app/models/billing/invoice.rb defines Billing::Invoice. A pack can own config/routes/billing.rb; draw :billing from root config/routes.rb. Keep tests in the pack and pass their paths explicitly to Rails test commands.

## Custom roots and moves

Honor pack_paths in packs.yml, including nested configured roots; do not infer ownership solely from the packs/ prefix. Create at the intended upstream path and use that exact path for dependencies. For optional Foundry scaffolding, supply --path=components/billing. Nested directories do not establish Ruby namespaces automatically.

`packs make_public PATH` moves code to the public path. `packs move DESTINATION_PACK PATH` moves code between owners. `packs rename` is interactive in 0.3.0; it does not take invented old/new positional arguments. `move_to_parent CHILD PARENT` and `move_to_folder PACK DIRECTORY` change topology. These commands can rewrite source, metadata and debt through upstream post-processors. Use them in a reviewed branch with a clean baseline and inspect every change.

After a move, review Ruby namespaces, references, routes, tests, public paths, foundry.yml, prompt lookup and .foundry receipts. Packs does not reconcile Foundry receipts. Do not edit hashes to make a generator accept moved code. Preserve the original receipt as provenance; explicitly relocate/reconcile owned artifacts with a disposable fresh scaffold when necessary. Verify fresh-process Rails loading and behavior before accepting the move.

## Checks and debt

```sh
bundle exec foundry check --sources
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec packwerk validate
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec packwerk check
bin/rails zeitwerk:check
bin/rails test packs/billing/test
```

Full Packwerk checks can boot Rails; use an isolated environment/database. `foundry check --boundaries` also verifies accepted debt bytes stay unchanged. Record behavioral tests separately from static evidence. Do not run `packs update` (update-todo) during normal no-new-debt checks. `packs lint_package_todo_yml_files` also invokes debt regeneration in 0.3.0, despite its name. Review formatting/move operations for writes; never silently accept regenerated debt. Use Foundry audit in a disposable copy to propose resolved-debt cleanup.

Upstream references: [packs](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs), [packs-rails](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs-rails).

module Knowledge
  class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

      Document.where(published: true).order(:id).map do |document|
        document.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')
      end
    end
  end

Record the starting revision, commands, actual outcomes, files/data changed and rollback

Domain commands under `app/application/billing/commands/` define `Billing::Commands::*`. Modular commands under `app/commands/billing/` define `Billing::*`. Models inherit the host's `ApplicationRecord`. Native operations inherit `Dry::Operation`, use `skip_prepending`, and establish one `steps`/`step` result boundary. Transactional commands inspect the failed result inside the transaction and raise `ActiveRecord::Rollback`. The generated savepoint prevents nested failed writes from leaking. Application callers decide whether a failed inner command also aborts their larger transaction.

Optional ROM writes must persist business state and outbox intent through the same ROM gateway transaction, with explicit rollback of failed native results. Deliver to RES or another destination after commit with stable IDs and idempotent recovery. dry-system is optional wiring and Trailblazer an alternative native workflow; neither warrants a Foundry container or result wrapper.

For existing-app extraction or persistence changes, read [adoption checkpoints](references/adoption-checkpoints.md). Verify characterization, caller boundaries and rollback at each relevant checkpoint; a completed assessment is not a completed migration.

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

    tenant = { 'tenant-a-token' => 'a', 'tenant-b-token' => 'b' }[request.headers['Authorization']]

require_relative 'test_helper'

class KnowledgeCatalogTest < BenchmarkTest
  def test_lists_published_documents_for_tenant_ordered_by_id
    second = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'second', revision: 2)
    first = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'first', revision: 1)
    document(tenant: 'b', body: 'other tenant')
    document(tenant: 'a', body: 'draft', published: false)

    rows = Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id: 'a')

    assert_equal [first.id, second.id], rows.map { |row| row.fetch('id') }
    rows.each do |row|
      assert_equal %w[id tenant_id body revision], row.keys.sort
      assert_equal 'a', row.fetch('tenant_id')
    end
  end
end

`app/` tree, remove `packs/knowledge`, and restore the root `package.yml` dependency list.
No migration or data conversion is required for rollback.

enforce_dependencies: true
enforce_privacy: true
enforce_layers: false

# Extract a knowledge boundary

Introduce a useful Knowledge business boundary without changing the existing /documents endpoint, tenant authentication, table or records. Expose Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id:) returning published document hashes ordered by id (id, tenant_id, body, revision). Delivery must call that API and must not access Knowledge::Document or persistence queries. Keep persistence internal to Knowledge. Existing public method signatures and unrelated jobs must continue working. For package-enabled applications move Knowledge-owned models/services/public API under packs/knowledge, configure enforced upstream privacy/dependencies and ordinary packs-rails loading; do not disable checks or add debt.   class RebuildSearch
    def call(index:, after_backfill: -> {})
      candidate = index.create_candidate
      index.replace(candidate, documents)
      after_backfill.call
      Document.transaction do
        index.replace(candidate, documents)
        raise 'candidate validation failed' unless index.valid?(candidate, documents)

        index.activate(candidate)
      end
      candidate
    end

    private

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

class KnowledgeBoundaryTest < BenchmarkTest
  def test_catalog_lists_published_documents_for_tenant_ordered_by_id
    first = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'first', revision: 1)
    second = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'second', revision: 2)
    document(tenant: 'b', body: 'other tenant')
    document(tenant: 'a', body: 'draft', published: false)

    rows = Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id: 'a')

    assert_equal [first.id, second.id], rows.map { |row| row.fetch('id') }
    assert_equal(
      [
        { 'id' => first.id, 'tenant_id' => 'a', 'body' => 'first', 'revision' => 1 },
        { 'id' => second.id, 'tenant_id' => 'a', 'body' => 'second', 'revision' => 2 }
      ],
      rows
    )
  end

  def test_documents_delivery_uses_catalog_without_touching_document_model
    published = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'policy')

    Knowledge.stub(:Catalog, Class.new do
      def self.list(tenant_id:)
        [{ 'id' => 99, 'tenant_id' => tenant_id, 'body' => 'from catalog', 'revision' => 1 }]
      end
    end) do
      rows = Documents::Delivery.list(tenant_id: 'a')
      assert_equal [{ 'id' => 99, 'tenant_id' => 'a', 'body' => 'from catalog', 'revision' => 1 }], rows
    end

    assert_equal published.id, Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id: 'a').sole.fetch('id')
  end
end

# Extract a knowledge boundary

Introduce a useful Knowledge business boundary without changing the existing /documents endpoint, tenant authentication, table or records. Expose Knowledge::Catalog.list(tenant_id:) returning published document hashes ordered by id (id, tenant_id, body, revision). Delivery must call that API and must not access Knowledge::Document or persistence queries. Keep persistence internal to Knowledge. Existing public method signatures and unrelated jobs must continue working. For package-enabled applications move Knowledge-owned models/services/public API under packs/knowledge, configure enforced upstream privacy/dependencies and ordinary packs-rails loading; do not disable checks or add debt. Plain Rails uses the same API and behavior in ordinary Rails directories. Foundry applications additionally record the focal context as modular in its pack-local foundry.yml. Keep workflow none. # packs-rails

`packs-rails` establishes and implements a set of conventions for splitting up large monoliths built on top of the [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) standard. `packs-rails` makes it easy to use [`packwerk`](https://github.com/Shopify/packwerk) to modularize your rails app. With `packs-rails`, new packages' autoload paths are automatically added to Rails, so your code will immediately become usable and loadable without additional configuration.

Here is an example application that uses `packs-rails`:
```
package.yml # root level pack
app/ # Unpackaged code
  models/
  ...
packs/
  my_domain/
    package.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    package_todo.yml # See the packwerk docs for more info
    app/
      public/ # Recommended location for public API
        my_domain.rb # creates the primary namespaces
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain.rb
      services/ # Private services
        my_domain/
          some_private_class.rb
      models/ # Private models
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model.rb # this works too
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model.rb
      controllers/
      views/
    config/
      initializers/ # Initializers can live in packs and load as expected
    lib/
      tasks/
    spec/ # With packs-rails, specs for a pack live next to the pack
      public/
        my_domain_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_subdomain_spec.rb
      services/
        my_domain/
          some_private_class_spec.rb
      models/
        some_other_non_namespaced_private_model_spec.rb
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_spec.rb
      factories/ # packs-rails will automatically load pack factories into FactoryBot, see Ecosystem and Integrations#factory_bot below
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
  my_other_domain/
    ... # other packs have a similar structure
  my_other_other_domain/
    ...
```

## Usage

Setting up `packs-rails` is straightforward. Simply by including `packs-rails` in your `Gemfile` in **all environments**, `packs-rails` will automatically hook into and configure Rails.

From there, you can create a `./packs` folder and structure it using the conventions listed above.

If you wish to use a different directory name, eg `components` instead of `packs`, you can customize this by configuring `packs.yml`. See [`packs`](https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs) for more information.

If you want to have your packs code namespaced without adding a directory with the pack's name into the directory structure, you can use the [automatic namespaces gem](https://github.com/gap777/automatic_namespaces).

## Modify spring to detect pack moves

If you use spring, when you move a pack, you'll want spring to update its cache

Add this to one of your initializers
```ruby
Packs::Specification::Configuration.fetch.pack_paths.each do |dir|
  Dir["#{dir}/package.yml"].each do |package_yml|
    Spring.watch(package_yml)
  end
end
```

### Splitting routes
`packs-rails` allows you to split your application routes for every pack. You just have to create a file describing your routes and then `draw` them in your root `config/routes.rb` file (NOTE: the `draw` function is only in Rails 6.1+).

```ruby
# packs/my_domain/config/routes/my_domain.rb
resources :my_resource

# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  draw(:my_domain)
end
```

## Ecosystem and Integrations

### RSpec Integration
Simply add `--require packs/rails/rspec` to your `.rspec`.
Or, if you'd like, pass it as an argument to `rspec`:

```
$ rspec --require packs/rails/rspec ...
```

Integration will allow you to run tests as such:
```
# Run all specs in your entire application (packs and all):
rspec

# Run just that one test:
rspec spec/some/specific_spec.rb

# Run all tests under the "foobar" pack and all the tests of its nested packs:
rspec packs/foobar

# Same as above but also adds the "binbaz" pack:
rspec packs/foobar pack/binbaz

# Run all test files inside the "packs/foobar/spec" directory:
rspec packs/foobar/spec

# Run all specs under the "packs/foobar/nested_pack" pack:
rspec packs/foobar/nested_pack
```

#### factory_bot and factory_bot_rails

Ensure you have the gem in your Gemfile, and that `require: false` is not present, otherwise the `packs-rails` FactoryBot integration will not be run upon application/environment load.
This integration will automatically add the `[spec|test]/factories` directory from each pack to the application's `config.factory_bot.definition_file_paths`.

Using the example application above:
```
...
packs/
  my_domain/
    ...
    spec/ # OR test/
      ...
      factories/
        my_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
  my_other_domain/
    ...
    spec/ # OR test/
      ...
      factories/
        my_other_domain/
          my_private_namespaced_model_factory.rb
```

#### rubocop-rails
[rubocop-rails](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop-rails) [targets paths](https://github.com/rubocop/rubocop-rails/blob/master/config/default.yml) starting with `app/`. You might need to override the `Include` globs to include your packs code.

Examples:
```yml
Rails/EnumHash:
  Include:
    - '**/app/models/**/*.rb'
Rails/InverseOf:
  Include:
    - '**/app/models/**/*.rb'
Rails/LexicallyScopedActionFilter:
  Include:
    - '**/app/controllers/**/*.rb'
    - '**/app/mailers/**/*.rb'
```

#### parallel_tests

`parallel_tests` has it its own spec discovery mechanism, so packs-rails's RSpec integration doesn't do anything when you use them together.
To make them work, you'll need to explicitly specify the spec paths:

```bash
RAILS_ENV=test bundle exec parallel_test spec packs/**/spec -t rspec <other_options>
```

#### Knapsack (Pro)

Similarly, Knapsack (and its Pro version) has its own spec discovery mechanism and the API will find and queue the relevant specs.
To make it discover your pack tests as well, you'll need to configure the following variables:

```yaml
KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_DIR: spec
KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_FILE_PATTERN: '{spec,packs}/**{,/*/**}/*_spec.rb'
```

Setting `KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_FILE_PATTERN` will tell Knapsack where your specs are located, while setting `KNAPSACK_PRO_TEST_DIR` is necessary because otherwise an incorrect value is sent to rspec via the `--default-path` option.

## Contributing

Bug reports and pull requests are welcome on GitHub at https://github.com/rubyatscale/packs-rails.

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        return :discarded unless current && current.revision == snapshot.revision

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

class KnowledgeCatalogTest < BenchmarkTest
  def test_list_returns_published_documents_for_tenant_ordered_by_id
    first = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'alpha', revision: 1)
    second = document(tenant: 'a', body: 'beta', revision: 2)
    document(tenant: 'a', body: 'draft', published: false)
    document(tenant: 'b', body: 'other tenant')

    rows = Knowledge::DeliveryCatalog.list(tenant_id: 'a')

    assert_equal [doc.attributes.slice('id', 'tenant_id', 'body', 'revision')], rows
  end
end

module Knowledge
  class PublishDelivery
    def call(delivery_id:, store:)
      delivery = Delivery.find(delivery_id)
      payload = JSON.parse(delivery.payload)
      DeliveryCatalog.list(tenant_id: payload.fetch('tenant_id')) if payload.key?('tenant_id')
      begin
        store.publish(id: delivery.event_id, type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload)
      rescue store.duplicate_error
        existing = store.read(delivery.event_id)
        raise 'conflicting event' unless existing == { type: 'DocumentPublished', data: payload }
      end
      delivery.update!(delivered: true)
      :delivered
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)
      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        current ||= snapshot

        Embedding.upsert({ document_id: current.id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                           version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector) }, unique_by: %i[document_id version])
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def call_job(document, version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [0.1, 0.2] })
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(
      document_id: document.id,
      tenant_id: document.tenant_id,
      version: version,
      provider: provider
    )
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_not_published
    doc = document(published: false)
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_tenant_mismatch
    doc = document(tenant: 'a')
    result = Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(
      document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'b', version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1] }
    )
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_changes_during_provider_call
    doc = document(revision: 1)
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.update!(revision: 2)
      [0.5]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_unpublished_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.update!(published: false)
      [0.5]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_does_not_overwrite_newer_embedding_with_older_result
    doc = document(revision: 2)
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(
      document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', revision: 2, version: 'v1', vector: '[1]'
    )
    result = Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(
      document_id: doc.id,
      tenant_id: 'a',
      version: 'v1',
      provider: lambda do |_body|
        doc.update!(revision: 1)
        [9]
      end
    )
    assert_equal :discarded, result
    assert_equal '[1]', Knowledge::Embedding.find_by(document_id: doc.id, version: 'v1').vector
  end

  def test_different_embedding_versions_coexist
    doc = document
    assert_equal :stored, call_job(doc, version: 'v1')
    assert_equal :stored, call_job(doc, version: 'v2')
    assert_equal 2, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_provider_errors_propagate_without_writing
    doc = document
    assert_raises(RuntimeError) do
      call_job(doc, provider: ->(_body) { raise 'provider down' })
    end
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end
end

  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

module Knowledge
  class EmbeddingJob
    def call(document_id:, tenant_id:, version:, provider:)
      snapshot = Document.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
      return :discarded unless snapshot

      snapshot_revision = snapshot.revision
      vector = provider.call(snapshot.body)

      Document.transaction do
        current = Document.lock.find_by(id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, published: true)
        unless current && current.revision == snapshot_revision
          return :discarded
        end

        existing = Embedding.lock.find_by(document_id: document_id, version: version)
        if existing && existing.revision > snapshot_revision
          return :discarded
        end

        if existing
          existing.update!(tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        else
          Embedding.create!(document_id: document_id, tenant_id: tenant_id, revision: current.revision,
                            version: version, vector: JSON.generate(vector))
        end
      end
      :stored
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def run_job(doc, version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(
      document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: doc.tenant_id, version: version, provider: provider
    )
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_not_published
    doc = document(published: false)
    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(doc)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_withdrawn_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.update!(published: false)
      [1.0]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_revision_changes_during_provider_call
    doc = document(revision: 1)
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.update!(revision: 2)
      [1.0]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_tenant_changes_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.update!(tenant_id: 'b')
      [1.0]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discards_when_document_deleted_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    id = doc.id
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      doc.destroy!
      [1.0]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(Knowledge::Document.find(id), provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_does_not_overwrite_newer_embedding_with_older_result
    doc = document(revision: 2)
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(
      document_id: doc.id, tenant_id: 'a', revision: 2, version: 'v1', vector: '[2.0]'
    )
    doc.update!(revision: 1)

    assert_equal :discarded, run_job(doc, provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    assert_equal '[2.0]', Knowledge::Embedding.find_by(document_id: doc.id, version: 'v1').vector
  end

  def test_provider_errors_propagate_without_writing
    doc = document
    assert_raises(RuntimeError) do
      run_job(doc, provider: ->(_body) { raise 'provider failed' })
    end
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_different_embedding_versions_coexist
    doc = document
    assert_equal :stored, run_job(doc, version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [1.0] })
    assert_equal :stored, run_job(doc, version: 'v2', provider: ->(_body) { [2.0] })
    assert_equal 2, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end
end

require_relative 'test_helper'

class EmbeddingJobTest < BenchmarkTest
  def call_job(doc, version: 'v1', provider: ->(_body) { [0.1, 0.2] })
    Knowledge::EmbeddingJob.new.call(

    )

    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_revision_changes_during_provider_call
    doc = document(revision: 1)
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(revision: 2)
      [0.1, 0.2]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_document_deleted_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).destroy!
      [0.1, 0.2]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_document_unpublished_during_provider_call
    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(published: false)
      [0.1, 0.2]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_discarded_when_tenant_changes_during_provider_call

    provider = lambda do |_body|
      Knowledge::Document.find(doc.id).update!(tenant_id: 'b')
      [0.1, 0.2]
    end
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc, provider: provider)
    assert_equal 0, Knowledge::Embedding.count
  end

  def test_does_not_overwrite_newer_embedding_with_older_result
    doc = document(revision: 2)
    Knowledge::Embedding.create!(
      document_id: doc.id,
      tenant_id: 'a',
      revision: 3,
      version: 'v1',
      vector: JSON.generate([9.0])
    )
    assert_equal :discarded, call_job(doc)
    assert_equal [9.0], JSON.parse(Knowledge::Embedding.find_by!(document_id: doc.id, version: 'v1').vector)
  end

  def test_different_embedding_versions_coexist
    doc = document
    assert_equal :stored, call_job(doc, version: 'v1')
    assert_equal :stored, call_job(doc, version: 'v2')
    assert_equal 2, Knowledge::Embedding.where(document_id: doc.id).count
  end

    doc = document
    provider = lambda do |_body|
      raise StandardError, 'provider failed'
    end
